newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Parliament ratifies South Korea's OECD membership.
newsitem.headline: Parliament ratifies South Korea's OECD membership.

text.p: South Korea's parliament on Tuesday ratified the country's membership of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), officials at the National Assembly said.
A total of 159 members of the 299-seat parliament voted in favour of the joining of the OECD, while 101 opposed the move, they said. Two of the 262 members present abstained.
The ruling New Korea Party, which has a slim majority in parliament, won support from one of three opposition groups.

Seoul was invited to join the Paris-based club of rich nations on October 11, but opposition members warned the OECD could force South Korea to open its local markets to offshore competition more rapidly when its economy slowed.
Since applying for OECD membership in March 1995, South Korea has sped up liberalisation of its financial markets to foreign investors and pledged further reforms.
South Korea would be the second Asian member nation of the club after Japan, and the first from the region's newly industrialising economies.
